description: Health of Trickster's MySQL and PostgreSQL wire-protocol listeners (connections, logins, errors, query time, session routing) and of the native SQL cache engine behind them.

panels.title: MySQL active
panels.description: Downstream MySQL client connections open now across the selected backends, connections still in the handshake included. On a routed listener a connection is counted under its terminal backend only after it authenticates and is routed. Reads 0 until the first connection, which creates the series.

targets.expr: sum(trickster_mysql_active_connections{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}) or vector(0)

panels.title: Postgres active
panels.description: Downstream PostgreSQL wire connections open now across the selected backends, from TCP accept to teardown: SSL negotiation, startup, authentication and short-lived CancelRequest connections included. On a routed listener the connection is counted under the router's name, not the target. Reads 0 until the first connection.

targets.expr: sum(trickster_pgwire_active_connections{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}) or vector(0)

panels.title: Login failures
panels.description: Client logins rejected per second, MySQL and PostgreSQL together (error class authentication): an unknown user or wrong password at Trickster's authenticator or, on a PostgreSQL passthrough listener, at the origin. Geo ACL refusals are a separate class. A steady trickle usually means a client with stale credentials; a burst can be credential stuffing. Orange from 0.01/s (about one per 100 s), red from 1/s.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(trickster_mysql_errors_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", class="authentication"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) + (sum(rate(trickster_pgwire_errors_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", class="authentication"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Upstream errors
panels.description: Failures to reach the origin per second, MySQL and PostgreSQL together: upstream_admission (the backend's max_concurrent_conns origin-connection limit was reached and the client refused) and upstream_connect (Trickster could not dial or log in to the origin, including the origin rejecting Trickster's own credentials). Any non-zero value means clients are failing; red from 0.1/s. The protocol error rows break it down by backend.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(trickster_mysql_errors_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", class=~"upstream_admission|upstream_connect"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) + (sum(rate(trickster_pgwire_errors_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", class=~"upstream_admission|upstream_connect"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Route failures
panels.description: Sessions per second that a routed listener (a user router, or a MySQL session-balancing ALB) could not place, both protocols: outcome no_route (the user maps to no target and there is no default_backend) or unavailable (the chosen target is down). Those clients are refused. Always 0 without a routed listener; see the Session routing row.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(trickster_mysql_route_selections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend|", outcome=~"no_route|unavailable"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) + (sum(rate(trickster_pgwire_route_selections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend|", outcome=~"no_route|unavailable"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0))

panels.title: SQL statements
panels.description: Native SQL statements per second handled by the cache engine for the selected backends, all cache outcomes. MySQL counts only SELECTs the analyzer classed as cacheable (served from cache or relayed); PostgreSQL wire also counts every relayed statement; Flight SQL counts its statements. Driver keepalive pings are not counted. Native statements never appear in the HTTP frontend metrics.

targets.expr: sum(rate(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Statement errors
panels.description: Share of native SQL statements that failed (cache status proxy-error or error, reported with a synthetic http_status 500). It includes statements whose origin returned an error, such as a PostgreSQL ErrorResponse on a relayed statement, so clients sending bad SQL raise it too. Orange from 1 %, red from 5 %.

targets.expr: sum(rate(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query", cache_status=~"proxy-error|error"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum(rate(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query"}[$__rate_interval])), 1e-9) or vector(0)

panels.title: Cacheable hits
panels.description: Over the dashboard range, the share of cacheable native SQL statements answered from cache: (hit + phit) / (hit + phit + kmiss + rmiss). Partial hits count because a dashboard refreshing a range that ends at now is mostly phit, which still serves all but the newest rows from cache. Relayed statements (proxy-only) and errors are excluded, so this differs from the Caching dashboard's cache hit ratio. Red below 20 %, green from 50 %; no queries means no cacheable statement ran in the range.

links.title: SQL query analysis (Time Series Acceleration dashboard)

targets.expr: (sum(increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query", cache_status=~"hit|phit"}[$__range])) / (sum(increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query", cache_status=~"hit|phit|kmiss|rmiss"}[$__range])) > 0)) or vector(-1)

panels.title: Active MySQL connections by backend
panels.description: Open downstream MySQL connections per backend, counted from accept (before the handshake) to the final close. There is no listener label, so two MySQL listeners on one backend are summed. On a routed listener a connection appears under its terminal backend only after it authenticates and is routed; the router's own name never has this series. A backend removed by a config reload keeps its last value until restart.

targets.expr: sum by (backend_name) (trickster_mysql_active_connections{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"})

panels.title: MySQL connection events/s
panels.description: MySQL connection lifecycle per second. accepted: a client connected; authenticated: its handshake completed; at close exactly one of clean_close, forced_close (Trickster's shutdown or drain closed it) or handshake_failure (never became ready: bad password, geo refusal, TLS or handshake timeout, client gone mid-handshake). TCP health checks and port probes that connect and leave count as handshake_failure. On a routed listener a failed login has no event here, only an error under the router's name.

targets.expr: sum by (event) (rate(trickster_mysql_connections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: MySQL handshake failure ratio by backend
panels.description: Per backend, handshake failures over accepted connections, dashed lines at 5 % and 25 %. Load-balancer TCP health checks that open and close the port count as failures, so a listener behind such a check can sit near 100 % while serving clients well; the authentication and geo error classes show real login problems. Failures are counted at close and accepts at open, so a short window can briefly exceed 100 %. Direct listeners only: routed listeners never record failed logins as connection events.

targets.expr: (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_mysql_connections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", event="handshake_failure"}[$__rate_interval])) or 0 * sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_mysql_connections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", event="accepted"}[$__rate_interval]))) / (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_mysql_connections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", event="accepted"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: MySQL errors/s by class
panels.description: MySQL failures per second by class. origin_statement is an ordinary SQL error from the origin (syntax error, unknown table) on a connection that stays usable: the client's doing, and often the largest series. Admission: geo, authentication, route, handshake. Origin: upstream_admission, upstream_connect, session_replay, query_timeout, origin_query, session_state_lost. Client limits: query_size, result_limit, unsupported_command, protocol. handshake also counts TCP health checks and port probes that connect and leave. On a direct listener a failed login or geo refusal is also counted as handshake; on a routed listener geo, authentication and route carry the router's name.

targets.expr: sum by (class) (rate(trickster_mysql_errors_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: MySQL upstream and session faults/s by backend
panels.description: Only the classes that point at the origin or Trickster's connection to it, per backend (top 10): upstream_admission (max_concurrent_conns reached), upstream_connect, session_replay, query_timeout and origin_query (Trickster abandoned the origin connection), and session_state_lost (that loss killed a transaction or other session state). Client SQL errors, admission refusals and client limits are left out. Any sustained value means clients get errors: check the origin, max_concurrent_conns and the backend's timeouts.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (backend_name, class) (rate(trickster_mysql_errors_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", class=~"upstream_admission|upstream_connect|session_replay|query_timeout|origin_query|session_state_lost"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: MySQL mean query time by backend
panels.description: Average time Trickster spends on a MySQL text-protocol query (COM_QUERY), end to end: size and parse checks, cache lookup or hit, origin round trip and result streaming, early rejections included. The histogram's operation="connect" series is left out on purpose: it is recorded before every statement, including reused connections that take about 0 s, so it does not measure origin connect time.

targets.expr: sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_mysql_command_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", operation="query"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_mysql_command_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", operation="query"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: MySQL query time p99 by backend
panels.description: 99th percentile MySQL query time per backend (operation query only). The buckets are 50 ms, 100 ms, 500 ms, 1 s, 5 s, 10 s and 20 s, so anything under 50 ms is interpolated: a backend whose queries are all fast reads about 49.5 ms whatever their real speed. Trust it for tails above 100 ms; the mean and the within-threshold shares describe fast queries.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, backend_name) (rate(trickster_mysql_command_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", operation="query"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Share of MySQL queries within 50 / 100 / 500 ms
panels.description: Share of MySQL queries across the selected backends that finished within 50 ms, 100 ms and 500 ms, read directly from histogram buckets, so no interpolation is involved. A cached workload stays near 100 % at 50 ms; a falling 500 ms line means slow origin queries or large results. Gaps mean no queries in the interval.

targets.expr: sum(rate(trickster_mysql_command_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", operation="query", le="0.05"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum(rate(trickster_mysql_command_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", operation="query"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

sum(rate(trickster_mysql_command_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", operation="query", le="0.1"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum(rate(trickster_mysql_command_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", operation="query"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

sum(rate(trickster_mysql_command_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", operation="query", le="0.5"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum(rate(trickster_mysql_command_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", operation="query"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Active PostgreSQL wire connections by backend
panels.description: Open PostgreSQL wire connections per backend, from TCP accept to teardown, including SSL negotiation, startup, authentication and short-lived CancelRequest connections. On a routed listener a connection is counted under the router's name for its whole life, never under its target (MySQL does the opposite). There is no listener label.

targets.expr: sum by (backend_name) (trickster_pgwire_active_connections{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"})

panels.title: PostgreSQL wire connection events/s
panels.description: PostgreSQL wire lifecycle per second. accepted and closed are counted once per TCP connection, always as a pair; authenticated means the session was fully established to the origin and relaying began; cancel_forwarded is a client CancelRequest delivered to the origin, or an in-flight statement Trickster canceled because its client left. There is no handshake-failure event; use the error classes. On a routed listener accepted, authenticated and closed carry the router's name.

targets.expr: sum by (event) (rate(trickster_pgwire_connections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: PostgreSQL session establishment ratio by backend
panels.description: Per backend, authenticated sessions over accepted connections, dashed lines at 80 % and 95 %. CancelRequest connections are accepted but never authenticate, so clients that cancel often lower this without any failure. A sudden drop together with startup, authentication or upstream_connect errors is a real problem. Gaps mean no new connections in the interval.

targets.expr: (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_pgwire_connections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", event="authenticated"}[$__rate_interval])) or 0 * sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_pgwire_connections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", event="accepted"}[$__rate_interval]))) / (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_pgwire_connections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", event="accepted"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: PostgreSQL wire errors/s by class
panels.description: PostgreSQL wire failures per second by class: startup (malformed startup packet or handshake timeout), geo (geo ACL refusal), authentication (Trickster's authenticator, or the origin in passthrough mode, rejected the login), route (no target on a routed listener), upstream_admission (max_concurrent_conns reached), upstream_connect (dial or origin login failed), protocol (oversized client frame or unreadable origin stream) and cancel (unknown cancel key or failed delivery). Ordinary SQL errors from the origin are not counted here. On a routed listener startup, geo, route and authenticator rejections carry the router's name.

targets.expr: sum by (class) (rate(trickster_pgwire_errors_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: PostgreSQL wire upstream faults/s by backend
panels.description: upstream_admission and upstream_connect errors per backend (top 10): clients refused because the backend reached max_concurrent_conns, or sessions that could not be opened to the origin (dial failure, or the origin rejecting Trickster's origin_url or upstream_url credentials). These carry the target backend even on routed listeners. Any sustained value means clients cannot reach the database.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (backend_name, class) (rate(trickster_pgwire_errors_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", class=~"upstream_admission|upstream_connect"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Native SQL statements/s by provider
panels.description: Native SQL statements per second by provider label: mysql or greptimedb on MySQL listeners (the engine dialect), postgres (also for timescaledb), greptimedb or questdb on PostgreSQL wire listeners, and flightsql. MySQL counts only SELECTs classed as cacheable; PostgreSQL wire also counts every relayed statement. A backend served on both a MySQL and a PostgreSQL listener (GreptimeDB) reports both under one provider, so the two protocols cannot be told apart here.

targets.expr: sum by (provider) (rate(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Native SQL statements/s by cache status
panels.description: Native statements per second by cache outcome, stacked: hit (answered entirely from cache), phit (cached rows plus a delta fetch of the missing time range), kmiss (not cached yet), rmiss (cached, but not the requested range), proxy-only (relayed to the origin without caching, for example on a session that is not cache-eligible or as a plain PostgreSQL wire relay), proxy-error and error (failed). A growing proxy-only share means more statements bypass the cache; the SQL query analysis panels (header link) give the analyzer's reason.

links.title: SQL query analysis (Time Series Acceleration dashboard)

targets.expr: sum by (cache_status) (rate(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Native SQL mean statement time by cache status
panels.description: Average engine time per native statement by cache outcome (histogram sum / count; this histogram names the label status rather than cache_status). hit is the cache read, phit and the misses include the origin fetch, proxy-only is the relayed round trip. The gap between hit and kmiss is what the cache saves per statement. Means are used because the smallest bucket is 50 ms.

targets.expr: sum by (status) (rate(trickster_proxy_request_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (status) (rate(trickster_proxy_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Cacheable hit share by backend
panels.description: Per backend, the share of cacheable native statements answered from cache, (hit + phit) / (hit + phit + kmiss + rmiss), dashed lines at 20 % and 50 %. Relayed statements (proxy-only) and errors are excluded, so this measures the cache on statements it could serve. A drop after a reload usually means an emptied or resized cache. Gaps mean no cacheable statements in the interval.

targets.expr: (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query", cache_status=~"hit|phit"}[$__rate_interval])) or 0 * sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query", cache_status=~"hit|phit|kmiss|rmiss"}[$__rate_interval]))) / (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query", cache_status=~"hit|phit|kmiss|rmiss"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Native SQL backends (selected range)
panels.description: One row per backend and provider over the dashboard's time range: native statements, cacheable hits ((hit + phit) over hit, phit, kmiss and rmiss; red below 20 %, green from 50 %), proxy-only share (relayed without caching), error share (proxy-error or error; orange from 1 %, red from 5 %) and mean engine time per statement. MySQL counts only SELECTs classed as cacheable, PostgreSQL wire every statement.

targets.expr: sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query"}[$__range]))

(sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query", cache_status=~"hit|phit"}[$__range])) or 0 * sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query"}[$__range]))) / (sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query", cache_status=~"hit|phit|kmiss|rmiss"}[$__range])) > 0)

(sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query", cache_status="proxy-only"}[$__range])) or 0 * sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query"}[$__range]))) / (sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query"}[$__range])) > 0)

(sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query", cache_status=~"proxy-error|error"}[$__range])) or 0 * sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query"}[$__range]))) / (sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query"}[$__range])) > 0)

sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_request_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query"}[$__range])) / (sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", method="QUERY", path="query"}[$__range])) > 0)

panels.title: Session routing (user routers and session-balancing ALBs)
MySQL route selections/s by outcome
panels.description: Placements per second on routed MySQL listeners (a user router, or a session-balancing ALB over MySQL backends), one per successful password check, by router and outcome: selected, default (an unmapped user sent to default_backend), no_route and unavailable (no usable target; the client is refused). A session keeps its target for life. A session-balancing ALB produces only selected and unavailable. Failures carry an empty backend, so they show whatever Backend is selected.

targets.expr: sum by (router_name, outcome) (rate(trickster_mysql_route_selections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend|"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: PostgreSQL route selections/s by outcome
panels.description: Placements per second on PostgreSQL wire listeners mapped to a user router, one per authenticated client, by router and outcome: selected, default (an unmapped user sent to default_backend), no_route and unavailable. A failure the router reported as selected, default or nothing is recorded as no_route. Failures carry an empty backend, so they show whatever Backend is selected.

targets.expr: sum by (router_name, outcome) (rate(trickster_pgwire_route_selections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend|"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Route failure ratio by router
panels.description: Per router and protocol, the share of placements that failed (no_route or unavailable), dashed lines at 1 % and 5 %. no_route usually means a user with no mapping and no default_backend; unavailable means the mapped target is down or out of the pool. Ignores the Backend filter, since failures have no backend. Gaps mean no placements in the interval.

targets.expr: label_replace(((sum by (router_name) (rate(trickster_mysql_route_selections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", outcome=~"no_route|unavailable"}[$__rate_interval])) or 0 * sum by (router_name) (rate(trickster_mysql_route_selections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))) / (sum by (router_name) (rate(trickster_mysql_route_selections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)), "protocol", "mysql", "", "") or label_replace(((sum by (router_name) (rate(trickster_pgwire_route_selections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", outcome=~"no_route|unavailable"}[$__rate_interval])) or 0 * sum by (router_name) (rate(trickster_pgwire_route_selections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))) / (sum by (router_name) (rate(trickster_pgwire_route_selections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)), "protocol", "postgres", "", "")

panels.title: Routed sessions/s by terminal backend
panels.description: Sessions per second each router placed on each target (outcome selected or default), both protocols, top 10. Use it to check that users land on the intended targets and that a session-balancing ALB spreads sessions as weighted.

targets.expr: topk(10, label_replace(sum by (router_name, backend_name) (rate(trickster_mysql_route_selections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", outcome=~"selected|default"}[$__rate_interval])), "protocol", "mysql", "", "") or label_replace(sum by (router_name, backend_name) (rate(trickster_pgwire_route_selections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", outcome=~"selected|default"}[$__rate_interval])), "protocol", "postgres", "", ""))

list.name: datasource
list.label: Data source
list.description: The Prometheus-compatible data source that scrapes Trickster's /metrics endpoint.

list.name: job
list.label: Job
list.description: Scrape job(s) holding the Trickster targets.

list.name: backend
list.label: Backend
list.description: Backends with native SQL traffic (MySQL, PostgreSQL wire or Flight SQL engine series), plus the router names that routed listeners report connections and login errors under. HTTP-only backends are not listed.

title: Trickster / SQL Wire Protocols
